t: A fortified settlement stood at the centre of what later became Hanoi from the middle of the fifth century CE, under the names Tống Bình, Đại La and later Thăng Long, and Lý Thái Tổ made it the capital of Đại Việt in 1010.
The city kept its status under the Lý and the Lê, lost it to Huế in 1802, was renamed Hà Nội in 1831, and became the capital of French Indochina in 1902.
It was the capital of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam from 1945 and of North Vietnam from 1954, and in 1976 it became the capital of the unified Socialist Republic of Vietnam.
dyk: Lý Thái Tổ named his new capital Thăng Long, 'ascending dragon', after claiming to have seen a dragon ascending the Red River, and Hanoi's older names such as Long Biên and Long Đỗ also featured the dragon.
ev: A fortified citadel, later named Cổ Loa, is built in what later became Hanoi
The Trưng sisters lead a rebellion against the Han dynasty
The Tang general Gao Pian recaptures the city and renames it Đại La
Lý Thái Tổ moves the capital of Đại Việt to the site and names it Thăng Long
Lê Lợi overthrows Ming rule and renames the city Đông Kinh
The Nguyễn king Minh Mạng renames the city Hà Nội
Hanoi becomes the capital of French Indochina
Hanoi becomes the capital of the unified Socialist Republic of Vietnam

f.founded: In 1010 the first Lý emperor, Lý Thái Tổ, moved the capital of Đại Việt to the site of the Đại La Citadel and named the city Thăng Long; a fortified settlement had stood at the centre of what later became Hanoi since the middle of the fifth century CE.
f.where: On the Red River in northern Vietnam, in a region of monsoon-influenced humid subtropical climate with four seasons.
f.known: Thăng Long, capital of Đại Việt from 1010; the Temple of Literature; the Old Quarter and its 36 streets; the capital of French Indochina from 1902; the capital of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam; the capital of unified Vietnam from 1976
f.today: Hanoi is the capital of Vietnam and its second most populous centrally governed city.
